title: Rebels and the Raj: The Revolt of 1857 and Its Representations

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the common sequence of actions through which mutinies broke out and widened into a rebellion in 1857.
Interpret the evidence of communication, planning and collective decision-making among the sepoys.
Explain how pre-British rulers and local leaders came to lead the revolt in different regions.
Identify the rumour about the greased cartridges of the Enfield rifle.
Recall the other rumours, prophecies and omens such as the Plassey centenary prophecy and the chapattis.
Analyse why rumours spread in the context of British reform policies, annexations and missionary activity.
Explain the stages of the British takeover of Awadh from the Subsidiary Alliance of 1801 to annexation in 1856.
Analyse how the disarming of taluqdars and the Summary Settlement of 1856 turned taluqdars and peasants against British rule.
Explain the links between sepoy grievances and the rural world of Awadh.
Evaluate the limits of sources on the rebel viewpoint and interpret rebel proclamations such as the Azamgarh Proclamation.
Explain how rebel proclamations appealed to Hindu-Muslim unity across caste and creed.
Analyse the rebels' attack on symbols of oppression and their attempts to set up an alternative structure of power.
State the special laws passed by the British in 1857 to suppress the rebellion.
Explain why the British reconquest of Delhi and the Gangetic plain was slow and difficult.
Explain how the British used promises of land to break the unity of landholders and peasants.
Interpret how British paintings, cartoons and prints celebrated saviours and justified vengeance and repression.
Explain how nationalist art and literature presented 1857 and its leaders.
